description: Get to know the location and character of all of Germany's official wine regions
objectives.0: Identify all 13 regions on a map
objectives.1: Understand the key geographic features of each region
objectives.2: Recognise the importance of rivers in German viticulture
slides.0.title: Germany's 13 Anbaugebiete
slides.0.subtitle: A Wine Map from Ahr to Sachsen
slides.1.title: 🗺️ Why Are Rivers Crucial?
slides.1.content: German wine regions are almost entirely concentrated along major rivers. Rivers serve three vital functions: first, they reflect sunlight, increasing the heat the vines absorb; second, river valleys form microclimates that protect grapes from frost; third, the steep banks drain freely and force roots deep into the bedrock. This is why the Rhine, Mosel and Main rivers and their tributaries form the heartland of German viticulture.
slides.2.title: 🍷 Western Core Regions
slides.2.items.0.text: Mosel — the Mosel valley, with its steep slate slopes and the home of top-tier Riesling
slides.2.items.1.text: Rheingau — the south bank of the Rhine, a traditional aristocratic region
slides.2.items.2.text: Rheinhessen — Germany's largest region, with diverse varieties
slides.2.items.3.text: Nahe — varied rocky geology, mineral-driven Riesling
slides.2.items.4.text: Ahr — the most famous Spätburgunder red wine region
slides.2.items.5.text: Mittelrhein — the Rhine gorge with its castle landscape; small-scale fine wines
slides.3.title: ☀️ Southern and Other Regions
slides.3.items.0.text: Pfalz — the warm south, balancing red and white
slides.3.items.1.text: Baden — the southernmost and warmest region, approaching a Mediterranean style
slides.3.items.2.text: Württemberg — Trollinger red wine country around Stuttgart
slides.3.items.3.text: Franken — home of the Bocksbeutel and Silvaner
slides.3.items.4.text: Hessische Bergstrasse — one of Germany's smallest regions
slides.3.items.5.text: Saale-Unstrut & Sachsen — two East German regions, continental climate

slides.5.title: 🌍 Interactive Guide to Germany's 13 Major Regions
slides.5.description: Click any region for details. Germany's wine regions split into three categories: 'Classic Riesling Core' — 5 regions (Mosel/Rheingau/Pfalz/Nahe/Rheinhessen); 'Warm South' — 4 regions (Baden/Württemberg/Franken/Hessische Bergstraße); 'Cool North/East' — 4 regions (Ahr/Mittelrhein/Saale-Unstrut/Sachsen).
slides.6.title: Quick Quiz
slides.6.questions.0.question: What is Germany's largest wine region?
slides.6.questions.0.explanation: Rheinhessen is Germany's largest wine region by area — over 27,000 hectares of vineyards and the most diverse plantings of any region.
slides.6.questions.1.question: Which river is most important to German wine?
slides.6.questions.1.explanation: The Rhine is Germany's most important wine river. Together with its tributaries — the Mosel, Nahe and Main — it concentrates the country's finest wine regions along its banks.
slides.6.questions.2.question: In the 'germany-regions-overview' interactive, which region belongs to the 'Cool North/East' category?
slides.6.questions.2.explanation: Sachsen lies in Germany's far east and is one of the country's most northerly regions. Together with Ahr, Mittelrhein and Saale-Unstrut it forms the 'Cool North/East' group of 4 regions. Pfalz and Baden are the warm south, while Rheinhessen is part of the classic Riesling core.
